title: FIXME marker in a script comment
description: Unfinished-work rule — a comment step in a script carries a FIXME marker (FIXME, FIX ME, FIX IT, FIXIT). A FIXME states a known defect that was shipped, which is why this rule is a warning while its TODO sibling (script_comment_todo) is neutral. Matching is case-insensitive and tolerates a separator, so the marker is found whatever notation the developer used.
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: FIXME is the developer's own admission that something is broken. Unlike a TODO it does not describe planned work but a defect that is live in the solution — every one of these lines is a bug someone already found and did not fix.
rule.remediation: Fix the defect and remove the marker, or turn it into a tracker issue and replace the comment with the issue reference. A FIXME that survives a release cycle is a defect nobody owns.

meta.description: Unfinished-work rule — a comment step carries a FIXME marker. Detector canon of the family: (?i)\bfix[\s\-_]?(it|me)\b, verified by tools/tests/rules/unfinished_work_detector.sql. Overlap with script_comment_todo is intended: a comment line carrying both markers is counted by both rules, so the sum of the two rules can exceed the number of marked lines.
